notes:
Lead inbound from code-assistant startup building in-editor code completions and multi-file context search. Typical flow: user opens editor -> entire repo/selection is used as context (very long). Current pain: OpenAI rate limits and cost for long-context sessions; want predictable unit economics. Interested in hosted API as quick unblock (self-serve trial).

Key requirements / asks (paraphrase):
- Support for long context (document-level & repo-level), efficient embeddings for search across repos.
- Clarify rate limits and burst behavior; need per-org adjustable limits or clear upgrade path.
- SDKs: they asked specifically for first-class Node/TypeScript SDK examples for streaming edits & delta updates.
- Security: SSO (SAML) for admin console in next quarter; audit logs required for enterprise customers but not blocking initial POC.

Notes from technical call:
- They plan to batch many small edits into a single request path to reduce tokens. Interested in prefix/KV caching to save cost.
- Sequence lengths: up to ~200k tokens across multiple files; looking for guidance on splitting strategies and reranking w/ embeddings for recall.
- Concern: server-side rate limiting caused dropped completions in their alpha; wants guaranteed burst capacity or graceful backoff knobs.

Next actions: send trial creds scoped to higher token limit for POC, attach Node/TS SDK sample repo, provide explicit rate-limit doc + recommended batching patterns. Follow-up demo scheduled 2026-03-10 with CTO.

Quoted from founder on call: 'We need predictable latency for IDE workflows  users won't tolerate a spinner.'
